terms.de: Wörter, die näher bestimmen und zeigen

en.title: Words that modify and point
en.summary: Adverbs tell how, when, where or how much, and demonstratives point to things.

paragraphs: An adverb adds information to a verb, an adjective or another adverb. It tells how, when, where or how much. A demonstrative, such as this or that, points to something and shows whether it is near or far. Both classes make a sentence more specific.

Many English adverbs end in -ly, made from an adjective: slow, slowly. But not all adverbs end in -ly, and some adjectives do: friendly, lovely. Demonstratives change for number. This and that are singular, these and those are plural.

SingularPlural
this bookthese books

this one (near)these ones
that one (far)those ones
here / there(adverbs, no change)

paragraphs: Fast, hard, late and early are both adjectives and adverbs: a fast car, drive fast. Good is an adjective, and its adverb is well, not goodly. Hardly and lately exist, but they have different meanings from hard and late.

Adverbs of manner usually come after the verb or the object. Adverbs of time can stand at the start or the end of the sentence. Adverbs of degree such as very and quite come before the word they modify.

items: Wrong: **She sings beautiful.** Right: **She sings beautifully.**
Wrong: **These book is mine.** Right: **This book is mine.**
Wrong: **He drives fastly.** Right: **He drives fast.**

ro.title: Cuvinte care precizează și arată
ro.summary: Adverbele arată cum, când sau unde are loc o acțiune, iar demonstrativele indică obiecte sau persoane.

paragraphs: Unele cuvinte dau detalii despre o acțiune. Ele se numesc adverbe și arată timpul, locul sau modul. Alte cuvinte arată direct spre un lucru sau o persoană. Acestea se numesc cuvinte demonstrative.

Adverbele nu își schimbă forma niciodată. Multe adverbe au aceeași formă ca adjectivele la masculin singular. În schimb, demonstrativele își schimbă forma după gen și număr. Ele arată dacă un obiect este aproape sau departe.
